summary: Interim (19:33 UTC). No confirmed unauthorized access yet. Internet scanning only: SSH brute force, WordPress/Grafana path-traversal probes (all 404). Weaknesses found and fixed on web-01: (1) jpark (Jun Park, contractor, not in staff.txt) was in the sudo group. Removed from sudo, locked, shell set to nologin. Only failed logins were seen against it. (2) deploy had NOPASSWD sudo for /usr/bin/rsync, a root escalation. Rule removed; CI uses only larkspur-deploy. (3) /var/www/internal/maint.d (steps ci-01 can fetch) could be written by deploy/www-data. Now owned by root, mode 644. (4) nginx ran PHP inside wp-content/uploads. Now denied. (5) larkspur-orders (root cron) eval'd values from the deploy-owned wp-config.php. Rewritten without eval. (6) larkspur-mailing-export (root via sudo) wrote and chowned files in the caller's home folder, so a symlink could redirect it. Now it builds the file in a root-only folder and renames it into place. Still open and being checked: 64.227.126.70 (DigitalOcean) logs in as deploy with the password every 4–6h across the whole 14-day log (short sessions, no sudo; looks like an old script). The deploy password is the same as the SMTP password in /etc/grafana/grafana.ini.

Update 19:37 UTC. No sign that anyone got in without authorization. Every successful login matches a staff key or password from that person's usual networks, CI (10.20.0.30), or the old monitoring box. 64.227.126.70 logs in to deploy with the password every 4–6h; rotate-secret lists "the old monitoring box" as a holder of that password, so this is expected. nvega's nv-x13 key was also used from 75.130.209.8 (a residential ISP) and hopped to db-01 for his usual checks (ls on the backups, service status). I'm treating that as nvega. Internet traffic was scanning only: SSH brute force, WPScan, Grafana CVE-2021-43798 traversal attempts (all 404). Nothing that needs a secret rotation.
Weaknesses fixed:
web-01: (1) jpark (contractor, not in staff.txt) was in the sudo group and a WordPress administrator. Unix account locked and removed from sudo; WordPress role set to subscriber, password reset, sessions ended. (2) deploy's NOPASSWD rsync sudo rule (a path to root) removed. (3) /var/www/internal/maint.d (maintenance steps for ci-01) was writable by deploy/www-data; now root-owned. (4) PHP execution blocked under wp-content/uploads. (5) mu-plugin agency-support.php (Blue Ridge Web Co.) answered without login: ?asup=env leaked DB details, ?asup=purge deleted files. Moved to /root/disabled; the logs show it was never used. (6) larkspur-orders (root) no longer evals values from the deploy-owned wp-config.php. (7) larkspur-mailing-export is symlink-safe (builds the file in a root-only folder, then renames it into place); id look-ups capped at 50 customers. (8) DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT set to true.
ci-01: jpark locked. The maintenance job's git gc ran as root in a repository whose hooks and config the developers group can write; it now runs as deploy. The repo config holding the GitHub token was world-readable; now 660. The backups key from db-01 is limited to write-only rrsync into /srv/backups (tested).
db-01: the dump job no longer puts the Redis password on the command line.
All jobs checked after the changes: release, maintenance, orders, payouts, report, dumps, mailing export.
Not changed, recommended: Grafana 8.3.1 is public on :3000 (upgrade when the mirror has a newer version). grafana.ini reuses the deploy password as the SMTP password. Password SSH logins are allowed on every host. Unused old keys: agarcia "work-laptop-old", tbrooks "old-laptop". The invoices job marks any invoice older than 21 days as paid, and the payout batch then pays it out.

COMPROMISE (updated 19:43 UTC). Someone holding Nico Vega's (nvega) stolen SSH private keys logged in and destroyed the shop's backups.
What happened: 75.130.209.8, an IP nvega had never used, logged in to web-01 with nvega's nv-x13 key at 19:27, 19:31 and 19:37. Each time nvega's real IP (108.21.239.27, in the logs for 14 days) was connected at the same moment. From web-01 the sessions hopped to db-01. At 19:37:45 they ran sudo find /var/backups/larkspur -mtime +7 -delete and, 4 ms later, -mtime -8 -delete, wiping every local dump and nightly archive. At 19:41:01 the attacker returned from 107.77.210.246 with nvega's pixel-7 key, hopped to ci-01 with the nv-x13 key, and at 19:41:04 deleted all of /srv/backups/larkspur the same way. nvega's NOPASSWD sudo gave the attacker root on all three hosts. Every sudo command is logged; the attacker ran only service status, ls on the backup folders, and the deletes. No secret files were read, so I rotated no secrets. Earlier nvega logins today from 172.58.77.143 (17:03, 18:49) ran only his usual read-only checks; treat them as uncertain.
Containment: on all three hosts the nvega account is expired and locked, removed from sudo, its authorized_keys disabled (saved in /root), and all its sessions killed. 75.130.209.8 and 107.77.210.246 are dropped by iptables on web-01. Nico needs new keys, generated on a clean device, before Maria turns his access back on. Assume his laptop and phone (nv-x13, pixel-7, and possibly macbook-2019) are compromised.
Recovery: the encrypted daily archives in db-01:/var/backups (18:50–19:40) survived. I copied them back to ci-01:/srv/backups/larkspur, and the dumps every 10 minutes are working again. The deleted nightly archives (Oct 31–Nov 11) are lost unless the offsite bucket has them (ci-01's offsite job has been failing: no route to Wasabi).
Weaknesses fixed: web-01: jpark (not in staff.txt) removed from sudo and locked, and demoted from WordPress admin. deploy's NOPASSWD rsync sudo rule removed. maint.d made root-owned. PHP blocked in uploads. The unauthenticated agency-support mu-plugin removed. eval removed from the root job larkspur-orders. larkspur-mailing-export made symlink-safe, with id look-ups capped at 50. DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT=true. ci-01: jpark locked. git gc in the maintenance job runs as deploy, not root. Repo config (GitHub token) no longer world-readable. The backups key is limited to write-only rrsync. db-01: the Redis password is no longer passed on the command line.
Checked and still working: release every 3 minutes, dumps to ci-01, payouts, orders, report, exports.
Recommended: require a password for sudo (all hosts use NOPASSWD ALL, which turned one stolen key into root everywhere); keep backups somewhere sudo users cannot delete; fix the offsite upload; upgrade Grafana 8.3.1; stop reusing the deploy password as the Grafana SMTP password. 64.227.126.70 (deploy password logins) is the old monitoring box and is expected.

COMPROMISE, final (19:46 UTC). Someone holding nvega's (Nico Vega's) stolen SSH private keys, nv-x13 and pixel-7, used his NOPASSWD sudo to destroy the shop's backups.
Timeline: 75.130.209.8 logged in to web-01 as nvega (nv-x13 key) at 19:27, 19:31 and 19:37, while nvega's real IP 108.21.239.27 was connected at the same time. It hopped to db-01, and at 19:37:45 ran sudo find /var/backups/larkspur -mtime +7 -delete, then -mtime -8 -delete, wiping every dump and nightly there. At 19:41:01, from 107.77.210.246 (pixel-7 key on web-01, then the nv-x13 key to ci-01), it did the same to ci-01:/srv/backups/larkspur at 19:41:04. 174.62.5.145 tried the nv-x13 key at 19:44–19:45 and was refused. Every sudo command is logged and the attacker ran only service status, ls on the backup folders, and the deletes. No secret files were read, so I rotated no secrets.
Containment: on web-01, db-01 and ci-01 the nvega account is expired and locked, removed from sudo, authorized_keys moved to /root/nvega.authorized_keys.disabled, and all sessions killed. 75.130.209.8, 107.77.210.246 and 174.62.5.145 are dropped by iptables on web-01, but disabling the keys is what actually closes the hole. Before Nico gets access back he needs new keys made on a clean device. Treat his laptop and phone as compromised. Nico's own failed logins from 108.21.239.27 since then are expected.
Recovery: the encrypted daily archives in db-01:/var/backups (18:50–19:40) survived. I copied them back to ci-01, and the dumps every 10 minutes keep landing there. The nightly archives from Oct 31 to Nov 11 are gone unless the offsite bucket has them (ci-01's offsite job has been failing: no route to Wasabi).
Other weaknesses fixed: web-01: jpark (not in staff.txt) removed from sudo, locked, and demoted from WordPress admin. deploy's NOPASSWD rsync sudo rule removed. /var/www/internal/maint.d made root-owned. PHP blocked under uploads. Unauthenticated mu-plugin agency-support.php removed (it leaked DB details and could delete files). eval removed from the root job larkspur-orders. larkspur-mailing-export made symlink-safe, with id look-ups capped at 50. DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT=true. ci-01: jpark locked. The maintenance git gc runs as deploy instead of root. Repo config (GitHub token) no longer world-readable. The backups key is limited to write-only rrsync. db-01: the Redis password is no longer passed on the command line.
Checked at 19:45 and working: release every 3 minutes, dumps to ci-01, the payout check, today's 19:44 payout batch (10 sent), orders, report, staff logins.
Recommended: drop NOPASSWD ALL sudo, which turned one stolen key into root on every host; keep backups where sudo users cannot delete them; fix the offsite upload; upgrade Grafana 8.3.1; stop reusing the deploy password as the Grafana SMTP password. 64.227.126.70 (deploy password logins) is the old monitoring box and is expected.
